{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested:
#   --job-name=job_wgpu
#   --open-mode=append
#   --output=./%j_%x.out
#   --error=./%j_%x.err
#   --export=ALL
#   --time=00:10:00
#   --gres=gpu:1
#   --mem=64G
#   -c 4

flux alloc \
  -n 1 \
  -c 4 \
  --gpus=1 \
  --time=10m \
  bash -lc '

# Slurm --open-mode=append: approximate by appending to existing files.
# Slurm %j/%x: approximate with Flux job id and a fixed jobname string.
exec >>"./${FLUX_JOB_ID}_job_wgpu.out" 2>>"./${FLUX_JOB_ID}_job_wgpu.err"

# NOTE: Slurm --mem=64G has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without a memory request/limit, the job may be placed where less memory is available,
# increasing risk of OOM or contention.

# NOTE: Slurm --job-name=job_wgpu is not expressed here as a portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

# Slurm --export=ALL: environment is typically inherited by the shell here.

singularity exec --nv --overlay "$SCRATCH/overlay-50G-10M.ext3:ro" \
  /scratch/work/public/singularity/cuda10.1-cudnn7-devel-ubuntu18.04-20201207.sif \
  /bin/bash -lc "

source /ext3/env.sh
conda activate

python ./test_gpu.py
"
'
"
}
